summary: The paper challenges the prevailing view that LMs retrieve bound entities purely via a positional mechanism, and proposes two additional mechanisms — lexical and reflexive — plus a quantitative mixture model that reproduces LM next-token distributions with high agreement (JSS≈0.95). Methodology is standard mechanistic interpretability (interchange interventions with carefully designed counterfactuals) applied cleanly, with a nice follow-up experiment (§3.4) that decouples the reflexive pointer from the answer entity, and a naturalistic-text extension (§5) that connects findings to 'lost-in-the-middle'. Weaknesses lie in scope: the causal-model quantitative results in the main body appear tied to one model/task (gemma-2-2b-it on music), some generality claims outrun the reported evidence, and statistical reporting is thin (single CI note, no seeds/significance across tasks). Overall, a solid, well-executed contribution to LM interpretability with a clear, useful finding.
strengths: Clear conceptual contribution: identifies two additional retrieval mechanisms (lexical, reflexive) beyond the positional mechanism established in prior work, and shows they are needed in exactly the regimes where the positional mechanism weakens (middle positions in long lists).
Careful counterfactual design that makes the three mechanisms predict distinct tokens under a single interchange intervention, allowing them to be disentangled empirically.

The follow-up counterfactual in §3.4 (answer token absent from original context) is a genuinely good control that rules out the most obvious confound for the reflexive mechanism, and the layer-ℓ vs layer-ℓ+1 comparison also refutes a plausible 'suppression' alternative.

Quantitative causal model (Eq. 2) with a Gaussian positional term and one-hot lexical/reflexive terms reaches JSS≈0.95, close to an oracle upper bound (0.96), and ablations show each mechanism carries load only in the regime the qualitative story predicts.

Breadth: 9 models across three families (2B–72B) and 10 tasks for the interchange experiments, with a naturalistic extension (interleaved filler sentences up to 10k tokens) that connects the mechanism story to the widely reported lost-in-the-middle phenomenon.

key_concerns.issue: The quantitative claim of '95% agreement' is showcased in the main text for a single model/task pair (gemma-2-2b-it, music). The abstract/conclusion phrase this as a general finding, but §4 explicitly notes the setup is run for gemma-2-2b-it on music with qwen2.5-7b-it additional-task results relegated to Appendix E. Without a main-text table across models and tasks, the reader cannot judge whether 95% is representative or best-case.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Move a compact cross-model×cross-task JSS table (means and CIs) into §4, and clearly report the worst-case as well as the average. If M is refit per model/task, state that; if not, evaluate transfer of learned weights across models/tasks.

key_concerns.issue: Statistical reporting is thin for a paper whose central claim rests on quantitative fits. Only a single line ('All CIs < 0.02; for M and oracle < 0.002') is given, and there is no report of seeds, permutation/bootstrap significance for the mechanism comparisons in Figure 2/3, or variability across the 150 interventions per (iP,iL,iR) cell. The interplay/'competitive synergy' claim in particular is asserted from mean logits without a test.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report seeds/prompt-sampling variance, add significance tests (or at least bootstrap CIs) for the ablations in Figure 5, and for the qualitative synergy claim quantify it (e.g., interaction coefficient with CI) rather than reading it off mean-logit plots.

key_concerns.issue: Positioning against prior work in the main text is compressed. Prakash et al. (2024, 2025), Feng & Steinhardt (2024), Dai et al. (2024), and Wu et al. (2025) are cited, but there is no dedicated Related Work section delineating exactly what is new in this paper vs. those (e.g., where Prakash et al. 2025's 'lookback' ends and this paper's lexical/reflexive decomposition begins). The reader has to reconstruct the delta from scattered sentences.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a short Related Work subsection (or expand §2) that lists the specific claims each prior paper made about the positional mechanism and states, per claim, what this paper adds, retains, or contradicts.

key_concerns.issue: Templatic-task generality: nine of ten tasks appear to follow the same 'X <verb> Y' clause template with fixed entity roles. The free-form extension (§5) adds only 'entity-less' filler sentences and doesn't vary syntactic structure of the binding clauses themselves. Claims that this establishes a 'general account of how LMs retrieve bound entities' are therefore stronger than the evidence.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either soften the generality claims to 'templatic binding tasks with filler-padded contexts', or add at least one experiment with syntactically varied binding constructions (relative clauses, conjoined clauses, discourse-anaphoric bindings).

key_concerns.issue: The Gaussian parameterization σ(iP) = α(iP/n)^2 + β(iP/n) + γ is a very specific functional form and its choice is not motivated or compared to alternatives (Laplacian, learned per-position σ). Since M's headline advantage over the one-hot positional variant (0.95 vs 0.85) depends on this smooth spread, its form matters.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Ablate the σ parameterization (constant σ, learned per-iP, other smooth families) and report which gains come from smoothing per se vs. the specific quadratic form.

key_concerns.issue: The interventions patch the full last-token residual stream at a single layer ℓ chosen per model. The paper acknowledges layer selection but the criterion is deferred to D.2. Without seeing it, the reader cannot rule out that the '95%' number is partly a layer-selection artifact.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Briefly summarize the layer-selection rule in the main text and report JSS as a function of layer (or averaged over a window) to show the result is robust to the choice.

questions_for_authors: How does JSS of M vary across all 9 models and all 10 tasks? Is the 0.95 number representative or the best case, and is M refit per (model, task) or shared?
In §3.4 you refute an 'absent-token suppression' alternative by patching at layer ℓ+1. Have you checked layers ℓ+2, ℓ+3 or later — could suppression appear on a different schedule than retrieval?

For the 'competitive synergy' claim (Figure 3, right), can you provide a quantitative measure of interaction (e.g., an interaction term in a regression of the target-token logit on iP, iL, iR positions) rather than an eyeball read of mean logits?
How do you disentangle 'number of entity groups n' from 'sequence length' in the middle-position weakening? App. G is mentioned but the main text should at least state the conclusion.

For the free-form-text extension, why does the positional signal *strengthen* while the lexical weakens as padding grows? Is this consistent with attention-distance decay hypotheses, and does the reflexive contribution change too?

Does the reflexive mechanism require the target token to be a single BPE token, or does it generalize to multi-token entities? This matters for how much the finding generalizes beyond short-name templates.
calibration_check: Mostly well-scoped, but the abstract/conclusion phrasing ('95% agreement', 'general account across 9 models and 10 tasks') outruns what the main-text tables actually demonstrate for the quantitative model, which is anchored to a single model/task pair; softening or adding cross-setting tables would fix this.

significance.justification: Meaningfully revises the prevailing single-mechanism view of entity binding in LMs and links it to lost-in-the-middle, a topic ICLR interpretability readers actively work on.

novelty.justification: The lexical/reflexive decomposition and the position-mixture causal model are genuinely new relative to the cited prior work on positional binding and 'lookback' mechanisms.

rigor.justification: Standard interchange-intervention methodology is applied competently, with a well-designed counterfactual and a strong follow-up control (§3.4) for the reflexive claim.

statistical_soundness.justification: Only a single CI remark is given, no seed variance or significance tests for ablations/synergy claims, and the headline JSS is reported for one setting in the main text.

calibration_honesty.justification: Most local claims are careful, but the abstract's '95% agreement' and 'establishes a general account' overreach what the main-text quantitative results demonstrate across models and tasks.

clarity.justification: The three-mechanism story is clearly laid out and Figure 1's illustration is helpful, but §3–§4 are dense, notation-heavy, and lean heavily on appendices for evidence a reader needs to assess the main claims.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard sections are present but Related Work is folded into §2 and is thin; the paper otherwise fits ICLR expectations.

reproducibility.justification: Task templates, counterfactual construction, layer selection, model list, and the mixture model's functional form are described, but critical details (layer criterion, per-model hyperparameters, seed count, whether M is refit per setting) are deferred to appendices.

related_work.justification: The most relevant recent work (Prakash et al. 2024/2025, Feng & Steinhardt, Dai et al., Wu et al.) is cited and used to motivate the delta, but no compact section delineates the contribution per claim.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative panels that directly support the claims — Figure 2's U-shape, Figure 3's diffuse-vs-one-hot contrast, Figure 5's ablation table, and Figure 6's padding sweep — with clear cross-refs to appendix replications.

breadth_generality.justification: 9 models × 10 tasks for the qualitative interchange story is broad, but the quantitative causal-model results in the main text are shown for essentially one model/task, weakening the 'general account' claim.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: a clear conceptual contribution with careful mechanistic evidence, held back by narrow main-text quantitative reporting and thin statistical treatment; fixable in a revision.
